interface.title: RTD Reactor Calculator
interface.field: UV disinfection / photochemical reactor engineering (environmental engineering, bioaerosol inactivation, chemical actinometry)
interface.stage_of_work: reactor validation and analysis: checking the flow assumptions, predicting dose response and back-solving kinetic or fluence parameters from measured runs
interface.what_it_is_for: Given a laminar-flow UV reactor's geometry, flow and fluid properties, it predicts survival (C/C0) with a residence-time-distribution (RTD) model and compares it with a well-mixed model, reports Reynolds and Peclet regime verdicts, and back-solves a microbial rate constant k or an actinometer fluence rate E' from measured C/C0.

data.note: The page opens with built-in defaults. The supplied rtd-calculator-inputs.json was loaded with 'Load inputs…' (L=19.7 cm, a=1.1 cm, Q=1200 cm3/min, k=0.87, Eavg=1.6, measured C/C0=0.00202, a 12-point sweep, wavelength 222 nm, sigma 1.32e-17, phi 1.0). Estimated k came out at 1.4659 and kp at 1.4752e-2, as expected. The load did not restore the batch C/C0 list. The file holds 3 values ('0.00202, 0.0221, 0.432'), but the form kept its 5 default values while the paired Eavg list became 3 values (1.6, 1.0, 0.1). This raised a count-mismatch error until I typed 3 C/C0 values by hand (screens/003.webp, screens/026.webp). The likely cause is that loading sets Calculation type, and the calc-type change handler then resets the C/C0 list (in-backsolve-values) to its defaults (static/js/calculator.js:102). The replay's note (check.json, t1) that the file itself has 5 C/C0 values is wrong. Saving inputs downloaded a JSON file (schema rtd-calculator-inputs-v1) that holds every form field by its element id.

features.name: Live parameter form with regime verdict badges
features.general: Edit physical inputs in a form and see derived dimensionless numbers turn into colour-coded pass, caution or fail verdicts on whether the model's assumptions hold
features.specific: Edit L, a, Q, µ, ρ and D. Uavg, U0, mean residence time, Re and Pe recompute after a short delay. Badges switch between Laminar, Transitional (uncertain) and Turbulent, and between Advection-dominated and Diffusion may be significant. Only the Diffusion regime (Pe) label tooltip gives a numeric threshold (Pe ≥ 10^5). The Flow regime (Re) tooltip only names the three regimes, with no numbers.
steps: type a reactor or fluid value
tab out so the debounced recompute runs
read the Re and Pe values and their badges
hover the Pe label to read its threshold rule
serves_tasks: Compute dimensionless flow numbers and decide whether the laminar, no-diffusion model applies

features.name: Bracketed root-finding back-solver with per-row status
features.general: Invert a forward model for many paired observations at once, with a search range you can widen and a clear 'unreachable' flag for rows that have no solution
features.specific: Paste paired C/C0 and Eavg lists (comma, space or Excel paste) and press Calculate to get k per row, or in Chemical mode E' per row. If the bisection bracket in 'Advanced: solver brackets' has no sign change, the row shows an 'unreachable' tag. Its tooltip names the bracket and says to widen the range in advanced settings. No banner appears for unreachable table rows; a bracket banner appears only for the single Measured C/C0 back-solve. Mismatched list lengths raise a count-error banner.
steps: paste measured C/C0 values
paste matching Eavg values (microbiological only)
press Calculate; the results table opens
if rows show 'unreachable', hover the tag and widen the lower or upper bound in Advanced: solver brackets
re-read the solved column
serves_tasks: Back-solve the rate constant for a batch of measurements
Back-solve the delivered fluence rate from measured conversion
Back-solve the rate constant from one measured survival value

features.name: Domain-mode switch feeding one shared engine
features.general: Choose an application domain from a dropdown so the form swaps its domain inputs and derived constants while the core model and shared inputs stay the same
features.specific: Calculation type Microbiological ↔ Chemical. Chemical shows wavelength, sigma, Phi, base fluence rate E' and MW. kp = sigma·Phi·J(λ) replaces k. D is estimated from MW. The back-solve table switches from k to E' and the sweep heading shows kp.
steps: choose Chemical in Calculation type
enter wavelength, sigma and Phi and read kp in the sweep heading
edit MW and watch D and Pe update
read the Calculated E' table
